scientific_hypothesis: Enforcing strict monotonic thickness progression during optimization will prevent layer inversion and improve spectral band separation compared to unconstrained chirped optimization.
expected_advantages: Prevents optimization from collapsing chirp structure
Better convergence stability than unconstrained gradient search
known_risks: Hard constraints may reduce feasible search space
May trap optimizer in local minimum if initialization is poor
Monotonicity may not be optimal for dual-band separation
expected_observations: If hypothesis holds: best_target_score should show improved average reflectance across 400-700 nm compared to route_01, with tightest_margin indicating broader band coverage
If hypothesis fails: best_target_score should match or fall below route_01, indicating chirp does not benefit this band combination
thicknesses_nm should show monotonic increase or decrease across the stack if chirp is utilized
stop_conditions: If best_target_score improves by less than 1e-3 against the historical best for two consecutive rounds, treat the axis as exhausted, stop and keep the current best
If chirp factor converges to 1.0 (no chirp), periodic design is optimal; stop and keep uniform thickness design
